 ‘You’ve got to show up’: Clay County kicks off early voting with nearly 6,500 ballots cast
 Ariel Schiller , News4JAX reporter , Jacksonville 
 Jud Hulon , News4JAX photojournalist , Jacksonville 
 Published:  October 23, 2026 at 8:29 PM Updated:  October 23, 2026 at 10:45 PM Tags:  Early Voting , Clay County , Vote 2026 ORANGE PARK, Fla. – Clay County residents turned out in large numbers Friday for the first day of early voting in the general election, with the county supervisor of elections recording nearly 6,500 votes countywide.
 At the Orange Park Branch Library, one of seven early voting sites in Clay County, more than 1,200 ballots had been cast at the single location by the end of the day. Despite the turnout, officials said the process moved quickly, with voters reporting wait times of five minutes or less.
 CHECK OUT THE VOTER’S GUIDE 
 “I didn’t realize today was the first day. I thought it was tomorrow,” said David Morrissette, who cast his ballot at the library. “But when I realized it was today, here I am. Let’s get in front of it.”
 Morrissette said he made a point to vote as soon as he could. 
 “I wanted to make it count on day one,” he said. “You’ve got to vote. If you don’t vote, you don’t have a say.”
 He added that he votes in every election. 
 “You’ve got a responsibility as a citizen to do it,” Morrissette said. “Otherwise, you don’t have a democracy. You’ve got to show up.”
 Kiva Smallwood, who also voted Friday, said the experience exceeded her expectations. 
 “We drove up, found a parking space, literally went right in,” she said. “It was pain-free.”
 Smallwood said she and her family had initially considered voting by mail but decided to come in person. 
 “It was more important to be here,” she said.
 A regular voter, Smallwood said civic participation is something she takes seriously. 
 “I think voting is important,” she said. “It’s a way to participate in your civic responsibility. Make sure that your vote counts. Always come out and vote no matter what.”
 Leonard Davis said the full parking lot at the Orange Park Library initially gave him pause. 
 “The parking lot kind of had me a little nervous when I first came up here because it was kind of full, but these people are really quick,” he said.
 Davis said a friend’s enthusiasm helped motivate him to head to the polls. 
 “Somebody reminded me, hey, go early vote. And she was energized and she was proud of her sticker, so I said, oh yeah, I got to do that,” Davis said. “You hear it every year that all elections are special elections, but this one actually seems like it’s very special.”
 Davis said he tries to vote whenever he can. 
 “I try and do my civic duty as much as possible, because if your voice isn’t heard, that means you didn’t come and vote,” he said.
 Linda Foster said she brought her granddaughter along to make the trip a teachable moment. 
 “I want her to know that it is a privilege that we have in this country,” Foster said. “All countries don’t have this privilege to vote, and I want to explain to her that it makes a difference. If you don’t vote and you’re gonna gripe, then you need to shut up. If you don’t like something, then you vote.”
 Foster also noted the stakes of this year’s election. 
 “I think this election is probably the most important one we’ve had in a while,” she said.
 Clay County’s seven early voting locations are open from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. through Oct. 31. Those locations include:
 Orange Park Library, 2054 Plainfield Ave., Orange Park 
 Health Department in Fleming Island Bldg. 600, 1845 Town Center Blvd., Fleming Island 
 Supervisor of Elections Office, 500 N. Orange Ave., Green Cove Springs 
 Middleburg Civic Center, 2102 Palmetto St., Middleburg 
 Keystone Heights City Hall, 555 S. Lawrence Blvd., Keystone Heights 
 Eagle Landing Residents Club, 3975 Eagle Landing Pkwy., Orange Park 
 Thrasher-Horne Conference Center, 2900 Thrasher Horne Ave., Orange Park 
 Election Day is Nov. 3.
